tob-10789: Theosophist and physician Franz Hartmann explores the borderland between medicine and the occult — mesmerism, healing by faith, the powers of imagination over illness. He argues that the old magical healers glimpsed real forces that materialist medicine ignores. The book is a curious document of an age when science and spiritualism still shared a table.
tob-13789: In this strange and famous work, Annie Besant and Charles Leadbeater claimed to use clairvoyance to peer inside the atom, describing the shapes they ‘saw’ decades before particle physics matured. Their drawings of subatomic ‘anu’ anticipated nothing exactly — yet the book fascinated scientists and occultists alike. It remains a landmark of Theosophical literature.
tob-4089: This Sacred Books of the East volume carries on Legge’s Taoist renderings — the later classics past the Tao Te Ching and Chuang Tzu. His notes unpack two thousand years of gloss. The book opened China’s mystic lore to English readers hungry for the East.
tob-4189: Edwin Arnold’s 1861 Hitopadesha turns the Sanskrit fable-book — shrewd beast-tales schooling kings in statecraft and readers in worldly rede. His verse-Englishing charmed Victorian readers. The book is India’s beloved worldly-wisdom. Read and retold these two thousand years, it has not grown old.
tob-9389: Halma’s Ptolemy gives the great star-book of olden days — the earth-centred heaven that ruled star-lore fourteen hundred years. His French rendering opened the work to latter-day readers. The Almagest stays the ground-stone of olden star-wisdom. Copernicus overthrew it, but its reckoning lives on.
cia-0000105889: From April 1965, a report on a senior Indonesian diplomat's belief that Jakarta would break diplomatic relations with an unnamed country — the truncated title keeps the full subject hidden. What survives shows Indonesia's foreign policy turning sharper and more confrontational. Even incomplete, the entry preserves a mood: a nation cutting ties as it radicalized.
cia-0000107289: A June 1991 assessment concluding that the prospect of living American MIAs was unlikely. After years of investigation, the judgment was that no U.S. servicemen remained alive in captivity in Southeast Asia. Short and sober, the document reflects the intelligence community's effort to close a painful chapter with honest findings.
cia-0000126889: A February 1968 report on Vice President Ky's intention to recommend something to President Thieu about a task force — the truncated title withholds the rest. Saigon's palace politics churned even as Tet raged. The entry is a fragment of the endless maneuvering inside South Vietnam's leadership.
cia-0000132289: Situation Report 598: skirmishing along the border, and Iraq fully something — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The ground war's opening skirmishes were the prelude to the rout. The entry is the border heating up: the first shots of the hundred-hour war.
cia-0000132589: A September 1960 report: Cuba and North Vietnam to exchange ambassadors. Two revolutionary states, formalizing their friendship. The document is the handshake, announced: Havana and Hanoi, aligned.
cia-0000135889: A 1954 contact report. The meetings went on. The entry is the contact: the source, met — the report, filed.
cia-0000136189: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for REELFOOT with a report received from ONTRICH on a Calligeris meeting — the truncated title cuts off the details. The meeting, relayed. The entry is the report: the gathering, described.

cia-0000136389: A 1953 cable on Guatemala withdrawing from ODECA — and reports that the USSR did not intend something, the truncated title cuts off. The regional break and the Soviet shrug. The document is the double news: the withdrawal and the indifference.
cia-0000138989: A 1946 military information report on Chinese communists supplying Russians in Korea. The aid ran both ways. The document is the reversal: the suppliers, supplied.
cia-0000139489: A 1954 report on conditions in POW camps, the attitude of communist personnel, and POW hospitals — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The captivity, examined. The document is the conditions: the camps, described.
un-ga-res-1889: General Assembly Resolution 1889, adopted in 1963. The early-sixties Assembly deliberated. The number and year are preserved; the resolution's purpose belongs to the text.

un-sc-res-989: Security Council Resolution 989, adopted in 1995 — aligned. The mid-nineties Council at work. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1189: Security Council Resolution 1189, adopted in August 1998 — the embassy bombings resolution, condemning the terrorist attacks on the American embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam. cia-0000132489: A 1960 CIA file on Cuba and the Caribbean — the archive number in parentheses marks it as one piece of a larger set. Castro's revolution was a year old and Washington was watching. The document is the watch: the island and its neighbors, filed.
cia-0000135689: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135689. The training year's records. The document is the record: the brigade, training.
cia-0000136689: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136689. The brigade's voice in Spanish, preserved. The document is the voice: the language, kept.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d89: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, November 2, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 89. Yet another that day. The message is the flood: the letters, many.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d189: The ambassador in the United Kingdom, Winant, to the President, November 4 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 189. London's embassy reported. The cable is the embassy's: Winant, briefing.

frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d389: President Roosevelt to Marshal Stalin, November 29, 1943 — Document 389. A third. The message is the tripling: the correspondence, intense.
a-book-of-golden-deeds-pg6489: Charlotte Yonge collected true stories of courage and self-sacrifice to inspire young readers — soldiers, sailors, nurses, and ordinary people who risked all for others. Each golden deed is told simply, as an example of character in action. Victorian children loved the book, and its heroes still have the power to stir the heart.
arxiv-2605-09089: A forged passport photo might be perfect except for one doctored field — the birth date, the signature. Abhishek Kumar, Riya Tapwal, Carsten Maple, and Mark Hooper detect forgeries at the field level in digital identity documents, localizing exactly what was altered. The 2026 paper is document forensics with a magnifying glass.
arxiv-2605-09289: Thin plates that do not fit Euclidean geometry — curved by growth or heat — vibrate in strange modes. Joseph C. Roback, Carlos E. Moguel-Lehmer, and colleagues study the dynamical geometric modes of non-Euclidean plates. The 2026 paper is elasticity theory for warped sheets.
arxiv-2605-09489: The signed bipartite graph SB(3,n) — with all its symmetries — cannot host a Hamiltonian cycle when n is even. Shisheng Li proves it with a clever sign-of-permutation argument. The 2026 paper is graph theory with a satisfying parity punchline.
arxiv-2605-10089: Lithium electrolytes — coordination, screening, emergent length scales — seen from a molecular perspective. Amaury Coste, Eva Zunzunegui-Bru, Ambroise van Roekeghem, and colleagues provide it. The 2026 paper is battery chemistry at molecular resolution. It sees battery electrolytes molecule by molecule.
plos-pone-0003389: Geneticists mapped the landscape behind a muscle-wasting disease in this 2008 paper. Facioscapulohumeral dystrophy (FSHD) is tied to shrinking repeat counts at the tip of chromosome 4. Using chromosome conformation capture, the team showed how the 4qA/B region rearranges the area's three-dimensional structure and regulates the nearby FRG1 and FRG2 genes, pinpointing how the architecture goes wrong.
plos-pone-0003489: Ecologists found earthworms rewriting the invasion rulebook in this 2008 paper. Diverse plant communities usually resist alien species, but the team showed that animal ecosystem engineers, like burrowing invertebrates, can flip that diversity-invasibility relationship. Their experiments reveal how belowground animals reshape who gets to invade aboveground.
plos-pone-0003589: Bioinformaticians Price, Dehal, and Arkin built FastBLAST for the protein universe in this 2008 paper. Comparing every protein against every other to find evolutionary relatives is enormously expensive, so their tool made homology searches across millions of proteins practical. The software underpins the hunt for new protein families and distant orthologs.
plos-pone-0003689: In 2008, Ghisovan, Nemri, and Shumikhina showed adult visual neurons can relearn their tastes. Cells tuned to one orientation shifted their preference after the animal practiced on a new target. The plasticity proves the mature brain's visual wiring stays adjustable, not frozen at birth as once thought.
plos-pone-0003789: Malavige, Jones, and Kamaladasa studied chickenpox striking adults in this 2008 Sri Lankan paper. Unlike in temperate lands, varicella zoster virus often hits grown-ups there with serious illness. The team linked viral load and T-cell responses to disease severity, mapping how the immune system handles a late first encounter.
plos-pone-0003889: In 2008, a survey exposed bullying in Pakistan's medical schools. Ahmer, Yousafzai, and Bhutto used questionnaires to measure harassment of medical students. The cross-sectional snapshot documents abuse as a regular feature of training, not a rare scandal.
plos-pone-0003989: In 2008, Lorkovic and Barta tracked a splicing machine's assembly in plants. The U1 snRNP matured with help from Cajal bodies and the nucleolus. The study maps where in the cell this gene-reading helper gets finished. The humble weed Arabidopsis proved a handy window into this universal eukaryotic process.
plos-pone-0004089: In 2008, a team watched immune memory form in real time. During vaccinia infection, effector and central memory CD8 T cells arose side by side. The two fates were generated together, not one after the other. The finding reshapes how vaccines may build lasting defense.
plos-pone-0004189: In 2009, Polouliakh, Nock, and Nielsen mapped the immune cell's inner switchboard. G-protein coupled receptor signaling in mammalian immune cells showed a bow-tie architecture. Many inputs funneled through a narrow core to many outputs. The neat blueprint aids drug targeting work.
plos-pone-0004289: In 2009, a team found learning's echo long outlasting its trigger. CAMKII proved needless for keeping learning-boosted nerve cells excitable. The cortex stayed excitable without it. The finding revises memory upkeep models today. Other kinases must carry the upkeep load alone.
plos-pone-0358589: Measuring blood flow usually ties up a clinician’s hands holding the device in place. This paper tests a clever workaround: mounting the probe on a Stifneck Select neck collar worn by the patient, leaving both hands free. The user study checks whether the setup stays steady and accurate — a small innovation that could make bedside circulation checks simpler.
plos-pone-0358789: Kidney cancer patients on immunotherapy after surgery live longer — but how do they actually feel? This qualitative study interviewed UK participants in the RAMPART trial about their health-related quality of life during adjuvant immune checkpoint treatment. Their firsthand accounts reveal the side effects and trade-offs that numbers alone miss.
plos-pone-0357989: Osteoarthritis grinds down joint cartilage as its cells fail. This study showed isoquercitrin — a plant flavonoid — eases chondrocyte dysfunction by targeting AKT1-driven control of mitochondria, the cell’s power plants. The compound kept cartilage cells healthier in lab tests, marking a natural candidate for slowing arthritis at its source.
plos-pone-0356689: Anxiety around childbirth doesn’t always fade after delivery — it can shadow mothers for years. This paper published a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis on the long-term course of perinatal anxiety. The advance plan sets up a rigorous synthesis of how anxiety evolves for new mothers over time.
plos-pone-0354989: Zoonotic diseases jump from animals to people — and rural Thailand sits on the front line. This protocol laid out a community-tailored One Health educational intervention to boost knowledge and practices for zoonotic disease prevention. The planned trial will test whether local tailoring actually changes daily behavior.
plos-pone-0357789: Drug-resistant staph is a moving target that keeps outrunning antibiotics. This retrospective study tracked methicillin resistance and antimicrobial non-susceptibility among Staphylococcus aureus isolates in Aseer, Saudi Arabia, from 2013 to 2024. The eleven-year trends show clinicians exactly where resistance is winning.
plos-pone-0357889: Astronauts need radiation protection — but developing new drugs takes decades they don’t have. This paper leveraged bioinformatics approaches for drug repositioning in space radiation protection. The computational screen hunts among existing, approved drugs for ones that might shield space travelers from cosmic rays.
plos-pone-0356389: Fear of happiness — the belief that joy invites disaster — is a real and under-studied phenomenon. This paper tested the psychometric properties of the Arabic Fear of Happiness Scale in a sample of Lebanese adults. The validation gives researchers a working, trustworthy tool for studying it in Arabic-speaking populations.
plos-pone-0357289: We look at the world differently when browsing freely versus hunting for something specific. This eye-tracking study compared the differential effects of free viewing and goal-directed search on visual attention. The recorded gaze patterns reveal precisely how purpose reshapes the act of seeing.
plos-pone-0357589: Science fairs teach more than science — they teach students to communicate it. This paper characterized high school students’ communication and presentation practices at science fairs and linked them to SEF outcomes. The findings show what the act of presenting actually teaches young scientists.
plos-pone-0347189: Brain monitoring should be comfortable enough for daily life. This paper designed and validated a modular smart headband with embroidered electrodes for comfortable EEG monitoring. The soft, wearable headband brings brain sensing out of the lab and into ordinary routines.
plos-pone-0343189: The tuberous sclerosis genes TSC1 and TSC2 harbor variants of sharply differing danger. This comprehensive in silico analysis examined non-synonymous single-nucleotide polymorphisms across both human genes. The computational predictions flag which variants most likely cause disease — prioritizing them for laboratory follow-up.
plos-pone-0345189: A humble nose bacterium may quietly protect children’s airways. This paper studied the presence of Dolosigranulum pigrum in the nasopharynx and its relationship with respiratory health status in the paediatric population. The microbe emerges as a potential respiratory guardian worth cultivating, not eradicating.
plos-pone-0355189: Exercise can prevent and manage breast cancer-related lymphoedema — but which components matter? This scoping review identified the core components of physical activity interventions for BCRL. The distilled components give rehabilitation specialists an evidence-based blueprint.
plos-pone-0348689: Nematodes of public health importance lurk in soil and water, needing systematic surveillance. This paper built a ribosomal marker-based metataxonomic framework for their environmental surveillance. The framework gives health agencies a standardized way to watch for parasitic threats.
plos-pone-0354089: Palliative care works only when the whole team reasons together. This Dutch participatory action research implemented palliative reasoning in multiprofessional palliative care teams. The study shows how shared reasoning improves end-of-life care — with patients, families, and professionals thinking as one.
plos-pone-0356989: Are multiple myeloma patients genuinely involved in their treatment decisions — or just informed afterward? This cross-country survey examined shared decision-making in multiple myeloma care. The findings measure the gap between the ideal and the reality, country by country.
plos-pone-0356889: Real-world data is noisy and lopsided — and ordinary classifiers choke on it. ASWBoost is a classification algorithm built on parametric exponential loss, designed specifically for noisy, imbalanced data. The algorithm keeps learning accurately where standard boosting gives up.
plos-pone-0355689: When IVF produces only abnormally fertilized embryos — 1PN or 3PN instead of the normal 2PN — should doctors transfer them? This retrospective analysis examined the clinical outcomes of 1PN- and 3PN-derived blastocysts when no transferable 2PN embryos existed. The outcomes data give fertility doctors evidence for one of IVF’s hardest calls.
plos-pone-0356789: This entry is a correction notice, not a research finding. It amends the paper on hepatitis B virus reactivation risk in treating HBsAg- and HBV DNA double-negative lymphoma patients. Readers should consult the corrected version for the accurate clinical record.
plos-pone-0353389: Edible cannabis impairs thinking and movement — but the hour-by-hour time course was unmapped. This paper tracked the acute effects of ingested cannabis intoxication on cognitive-motor tasks across six hours. The time series reveals when impairment peaks and fades — critical data for drugged-driving policy.
plos-pone-0355989: Pacific Peoples living with Parkinson’s — and their extended families, their āiga and kāinga — experience the disease through cultural lenses medicine often ignores. This qualitative study honored those experiences. The findings demand Parkinson’s care that respects Pacific values of collective family life.
plos-pone-0355489: Quilombola communities — descendants of escaped enslaved people — face stark healthcare access inequalities in the Brazilian Amazon. This paper associated those inequalities with social, organizational, and territorial factors in rural and riverside communities. The findings demand health policies that reach the Amazon’s most marginalized.
plos-pone-0355389: Dengue’s four serotypes complicate vaccines — but a consensus NS1 mRNA vaccine might cross-protect. This mouse study demonstrated cross-serotype immunity elicited by the consensus vaccine. The findings inch toward a dengue vaccine that protects against all serotypes without risking antibody-enhanced disease.
plos-pone-0355289: Traditional medicine practitioners in Ghana are often the first consulted about breast lumps — gatekeepers or barriers? This paper explored their understanding of breast cancer. The findings reveal whether traditional healers speed or delay the diagnosis that determines survival.
europmc-pmc2797089: Fly DNA holds insulator bits that stop genes from meddling with their neighbors. This 2010 paper charts these bits across the whole fruit fly genome. With genome-wide data, the team pins down thousands of such sites. The chart became a go-to guide for how the fly genome is laid out and run.
europmc-pmc2873589: Parkinson's damage may start in the brain's support cells. This 2010 mouse study shows astrocytic expression of mutant A53T alpha-synuclein causes neurodegeneration. The authors prove glia alone can drive the disease. Their work widened the search for Parkinson's origins beyond neurons.
europmc-pmc2875389: Tracking tuberculosis germs inside bodies needs glowing reporters. This 2010 paper tunes light-making reporter genes for use with mycobacteria, the TB germ family. The authors test which glow systems work best in these tough bugs. Their brighter tools let researchers watch infections unfold in real time.
europmc-pmc2879389: Species maps look complete but hide deep biases. This 2010 paper exposes spatial and temporal bias in species occurrence data, showing distorted views of biodiversity. The authors quantify how museum records skew toward roads and rich countries. Their warning matters for conservation plans built on patchy records.
europmc-pmc2883589: The brain wires near and far in patterns, and this 2010 paper maps them. The authors chart the organization of local and distant functional connectivity in the human brain. Their map reveals order in the wiring. The work aids reading healthy and diseased brains.
europmc-pmc2944089: Traffic fumes may raise diabetes risk for older women. This 2010 paper links traffic-related air pollution to new type 2 diabetes in the SALIA cohort study. The authors follow the women for years, strengthening the case. Their finding adds diabetes to air pollution's long toll on health.
europmc-pmc3002989: TB's eis gene meddles with the cell's cleanup and suicide programs. This 2010 paper shows the tuberculosis eis gene steers self-eating, inflammation, and cell death through redox signals. The authors map the meddling. Their work flags new TB drug targets.
europmc-pmc3009689: Sequence lining-up got evolution-aware. This 2010 paper brings webPRANK, a tool that lines up DNA using the family tree. The authors' program beats naive lining-up. Their software spread to labs worldwide. Gappy regions finally align with sense. Evolution guides every gap it places.
europmc-pmc3017089: Traditional Chinese medicine went digital. This 2011 paper builds Taiwan's huge database of Chinese herbal formulas for computer drug screening. The authors mine ancient recipes with modern math. Their resource aids drug discovery. Old herbs meet new algorithms here. The database holds tens of thousands of compounds.
europmc-pmc3026789: Brain immune cells dance to nerve signals. This 2011 paper shows brain chatter shapes the form and moves of microglia. The authors film the control in live tissue. Their work links neurons to their immune neighbors. Calm nerves keep the immune cells branched.
europmc-pmc3087489: Fly glia wake sleeping stem cells. This 2010 paper shows food-sensing glia rouse dormant brain stem cells. The authors reveal the wake-up call. Their work lights up brain development. Fed flies reboot brain growth fast. Starved brains stay on pause.
europmc-pmc6520689: Does eating three square meals beat grazing - or skipping breakfast help? This review sifts human studies on meal frequency, timing, and fasting. Population data link more frequent eating to lower disease risk, but controlled trials tell a messier story. The authors conclude that when you eat matters less than how much and what, though fasting windows show genuine promise.
europmc-pmc6619389: Cancer treatment forces a cruel tradeoff: harsher therapy may buy time but steal quality of life. This systematic review asks what patients themselves prefer - length of life, quality of life, or some balance. The findings give doctors a clearer window into patient values when planning care.
europmc-pmc6717989: Cytoscape draws beautiful biological networks - but clicking through menus does not scale. Cytoscape Automation wires the tool into scripted workflows, letting researchers build reproducible, large-scale network analyses. The upgrade turns a beloved interactive toy into pipeline-grade machinery.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-889: A papers-please rule was dropping the insured in 2007 — GAO's report says states blamed the citizenship proof mandate for enrollment slides among eligible kids. The findings document the paperwork purge. The report asks whether the fraud fight was worth the children it cut.
pmc-13466889: A 2026 materials science paper on making bismuth tungstate-doped geopolymers — a kind of eco-friendly concrete alternative — and testing how they break down tetracycline antibiotics in water under visible light. The green, low-cost synthesis doubles as pollution cleanup technology, since antibiotic runoff is a growing environmental problem.
pmc-13439489: This 2026 ecology paper found that fungal communities differ between floral nectaries (in flowers) and extrafloral nectaries (on leaves and stems). These sugar-secreting glands host distinct microbial worlds with different ecological roles. The study maps a hidden layer of plant-microbe interaction.
pmc-13459089: A 2026 endocrinology paper on using 11-deoxycortisol and other hormone measurements, plus pituitary function characteristics, to diagnose adrenal insufficiency in the overnight oral metyrapone test. The test is a workhorse of endocrine diagnosis, and the study refines how to read it. Better interpretation means fewer missed cases.
pmc-13499689: This 2026 paper derived a "urinary metabolic age" from high-resolution NMR spectroscopy of urine, revealing longitudinal aging patterns. Metabolic age from a urine sample could track how fast someone is aging biologically. The longitudinal data show the measure moves with time.
pmc-13524089: A 2026 plant biology paper showing that GH3 phylogenetic subgroups define divergent routes of auxin inactivation via aspartate and glutamine conjugation. Plants deactivate the growth hormone auxin by tagging it with amino acids, and different enzyme families take different routes. The evolutionary split is the insight.
pmc-13542589: In this 2026 animal nutrition paper, microbial-phytase co-fermentation of sorghum improved growth, nutrient use, digestive enzymes, and cecal microbiota (the title is truncated). Fermentation plus enzyme unlocks the grain's value. The feeding study gives producers evidence.
pmc-13468889: A 2026 engineering paper on pyrolysis gas generation from insulating oil under electro-thermal action, simulated with ReaxFF. Transformer failures release dangerous gases. The simulation predicts them.
pmc-13468789: A 2026 critical narrative review of advances in rehabilitation for bone and joint pain — evidence, gaps, and future directions. The review is honest about what works and what doesn't. The gaps point the way.
pmc-13530589: A 2026 conference poster finding equivalent 10-year outcomes after primary hip arthroscopy in patients with atypical hip pain from femoroacetabular impingement. The long-term equivalence is reassuring. The poster reports the decade of follow-up.
pmc-13448489: This 2026 conference abstract (BSLD-08) proposed MAL2 as a potential driver and prognostic marker of leptomeningeal colonization in lung and breast cancer. The membrane protein's role in brain lining spread was the hypothesis. The abstract presents the evidence.
pmc-13529189: A 2026 pharmacovigilance study analyzing acyclovir safety in neonates using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System. The antiviral's risks in newborns were mined from reports. The safety analysis is the contribution.
pmc-13548789: A 2026 oncology review on bone health in advanced prostate cancer — pathophysiology and management. The bone-metastatic disease needs bone care. The review is the guide.
pmc-13504289: A 2026 genomics paper classifying chromatin accessibility at TAD boundaries disclosed new architectural proteins. The boundary proteins were discovered. The classification is the method.
pmc-13469989: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of disease-free survival as a surrogate outcome for localized kidney cancer. The surrogate's validity was tested. The analysis informs trial design.
pmc-13465489: A 2026 analytical paper on an in-house fabricated one-step SPE cartridge with HPLC-MS/MS for fast, accurate determination of multi-class contaminants in eggs. The homemade cartridge worked. The method serves food safety.
pmc-13458389: A 2026 cell biology paper: ZNF512B associated with mitotic spindles, regulated metaphase exit, and proved crucial for stem cell differentiation. The protein's mitotic role was defined. The regulation is the discovery.
pmc-13453589: This 2026 oncology paper targeted spatiotemporal heterogeneity of oncomiRNAs — a new frontier in cancer therapy. The cancer microRNAs' variability was the target. The frontier is the concept.
pmc-13438189: A 2026 genetics paper on the role of polygenic risk in Alzheimer's disease prediction for African Americans. The risk scores' predictive power was tested in the population. The role is the finding.
pmc-13430089: In this 2026 narrative review, the gut microbiome and ADHD were examined — clinical evidence and practice implications. The gut-brain link's evidence was synthesized. The review weighs the claims.
pmc-13431689: This 2026 review covered sleep circuit modulation — from animal models to human translation. The sleep circuits' therapeutic manipulation was surveyed. The review bridges the species.
pmc-13472889: A 2026 sleep neuroscience paper: glutamate excitatory inputs to the sublaterodorsal tegmental nucleus are necessary for REM sleep — where are they located? The REM gate's inputs were hunted. The question drives the research.
pmc-13639589: In this 2026 retrospective cohort study of 1,651 hips, postoperative D-dimer-based screening for venous thromboembolism after total hip arthroplasty was evaluated. The blood test's screening value was tested. The screening is the protocol question.
pmc-13545689: This 2026 systematic review examined autologous fat-derived products for skin and scar optimization in rhinoplasty and nasal reconstruction. The fat grafts' nasal role was synthesized. The review guides plastic surgeons.
pmc-13517389: A 2026 mouse study on the possible role of gut microbiota in polypropylene microplastics-induced immunity and reproductive dysfunction. The plastic's harm ran through the gut. The role is the mechanistic hypothesis.
pmc-13441289: A 2026 clinical decision-making paper on acute ischemic stroke with large vessel occlusion. The stroke scenario's decisions were worked through. The paper teaches the approach.
pmc-13469589: In this 2026 cryptography paper, lightweight anonymous group authentication and quantum-cloud key distribution based on PUF were developed for classical network environments. The quantum-safe auth was the advance. The developing is the security contribution.
pmc-13467289: This 2026 correction notice amended a paper on thermomechanical treatment of Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloy with minor scandium and zirconium additions (the title is truncated). Corrections fix the record. This entry preserves the correction.
pmc-13457789: A 2026 prospective observational study comparing four commercially available adhesion barriers after open thyroid surgery. The anti-scar products were head-to-head. The comparison guides surgeons.
pmc-13427789: A 2026 paper estimating the minimal clinically important difference of functional outcomes in spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy. The meaningful change threshold was set. The estimating aids trial design.
pmc-13464989: This 2026 paper examined persistent low-level hCG after gestational trophoblastic neoplasia remission — treatment-free probability stratified by early hCG course. The lingering hormone's meaning was quantified. The stratifying aids surveillance.
pmc-13454989: In this 2026 paper, crocin I delayed cellular senescence potentially via modulating SIRT1/PKM2 expression to improve lactate homeostasis in vitro. The saffron compound's anti-aging mechanism was probed. The delaying is the finding.
pmc-13416389: In this 2026 case report, intrathyroidal parathyroid carcinoma was found in a multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 patient. The hidden parathyroid cancer was documented. The case teaches the differential.
pmc-13449989: A 2026 multicenter cohort study of intratumoral Fusobacterium species and survival in resectable colorectal cancer. The tumor bacteria's prognostic role was tested. The study is the evidence.
arxiv-2606-15989: Comparing brain scans across different people is hard because every brain is shaped differently. This paper builds a multi-encoder-decoder VAE — a neural network architecture — that lines up brain signals from different subjects around the task they are doing. The method helps neuroscientists find common patterns in brain activity despite individual differences.
arxiv-2606-16189: Prime numbers pop up in odd recipes. This number paper probes one recipe-line of a set shape, guessing rules for when its yields are prime, proving some claims on big 'if's, and nailing down prime proofs that need no ifs. For fans of prime hunts and math-code.
arxiv-2606-16789: The Satsuma–Mimura equation describes mixing groups — and it has elegant wave answers. This paper studies its 'pole dynamics': tracking the singular points of answers, plus how to straighten the equation and how it reacts to nudges. It is for applied math pros in wild waves.
